live_manifest.note: the same manifest every T2-T4 run used; receipt in runtime data/travis/t4-rulings/lexicon/receipts.jsonl

schemas_checked.proof: the schema bytes in the elephant-cli cache hash (raw CIDv1, SHA-256) to the CIDs the live manifest names, so the members below are the live schema

member_descriptions: none: the live class schema lists the enum members without per-member descriptions, so faithfulness is judged by the member name against the printed value
kit_precedent: skills/use-oracle/runtime/counties/pinellas/transforms/data_extractor.js mapImprovementType: printed "general building" -> GeneralBuilding, "mechanical" / "hvac" -> MechanicalHVAC, "electrical" -> Electrical, "plumbing" -> Plumbing, "driveway" / "driveway permit" -> DrivewayPermit, "right of way" -> RightOfWayPermit

top_permit_class: C- 329 Com Structures Other Than Bldg
R- 329 Res Structures Other Than Bldg
BP.finding: holds: one printed type, "Building Permit", on every row; GeneralBuilding is the generic building member. Coarse but not wrong: finer members exist (ResidentialConstruction, CommercialConstruction, BuildingAddition, Demolition, StructureMove) that only permit_class or work_class could select, which the code-only rule does not use

EP.finding: holds: one printed type, "Electrical Permit"; sign and solar work stays electrical at the type level

MP.finding: holds: one printed type, "Mechanical Permit"; the work is HVAC, ducts and hoods (gas named in 0.8% of descriptions); the kit maps "mechanical" to MechanicalHVAC

top_permit_class: R- 329 Res Structures Other Than Bldg
PP.finding: holds: one printed type, "Plumbing Permit"; irrigation and gas sub-scopes exist (LandscapeIrrigation, GasInstallation) but the printed type is plumbing

DS.finding: does not hold for every row: the printed type is "Driveway / Sidewalks"; 110,710 of 116,649 rows (94.9%) carry a permit_class that names a driveway, 2,452 name only sidewalk, curb or gutter work ({"Replace of Curb & Gutter": 9, "Com. Sidewalk": 841, "Com. Curb, Gutter": 96, "Res. Curb, Gutter": 112, "Res. Sidewalk": 821, "Com. Sidewalk, Curb, Gutter": 502, "Res. Sidewalk, Curb, Gutter": 71}), and 3,487 have no permit_class; DrivewayPermit would misdescribe at least 2,452 rows and is unproven for 3,487

verdict_improvement_type.why_not_applied: the ruling approved the five-code mapping on condition that it holds; DS does not map one to one, so nothing was written (the transform stays travis-permit-transform-v1, all four enums null)
options_for_the_operator: four codes as approved and DS null
DS by permit_class: classes naming a driveway -> DrivewayPermit, the rest null (no longer code-only)

DS -> RightOfWayPermit for every row, if mew confirms the member covers driveway approaches as well as sidewalks, curbs and gutters (all are right-of-way work in Austin, but the data does not prove every DS permit is)

partial_improvement_status.not_faithful: Expired (no member), Active (Permitted or InProgress: the export cannot tell whether work started), VOID (an administrative void, not necessarily cancelled work), Withdrawn and Aborted (ended by the applicant or the city, not printed as cancelled), Pending, Re Review, Suspended and the rest
partial_improvement_status.correct: yes for the five printed values above: Final is the finaled permit (the profile already reads only Final as completed work), On Hold and the three Cancelled values name their member
partial_improvement_status.better: marginal for this product: the hosted layer serves the printed status and its status_group from the run capture either way; it adds a CID-backed completion flag on 84.5% of the rows for Atlas and MCP consumers. Every later status change gives the permit a new record CID, as a new completion date already does

partial_improvement_action.two_actions_or_no_member: Addition and Remodel (69,748: two actions), Irrigation, Upgrade, Auxiliary Power, Wall, Homebuilder Loop, Shell, Relocation, Fireline, Life Safety and the rest
partial_improvement_action.correct: only the exact names are faithful to the printed field; Remodel -> Alteration, Demolition -> Remove and Change Out -> Replacement are readings, not names
partial_improvement_action.conflict: work_class is the filing category, not the work: Austin files re-roofs as Repair or Remodel (findings section 4), so a published improvement_action Repair would sit on 23,290 permits the profile reads as primary-roof replacements; an Atlas consumer would read a re-roof as a repair
partial_improvement_action.better: no: it would publish a value that contradicts the roofing signal on the permits that matter most for this product

readme_lines.105: Show properties in that area with open roofing permits, prioritizing permits that have remained open for many years
readme_lines.110: Which properties near that area have open roofing permits that have been open for many years

readme_open_permit_questions.answered_from: the printed status_current of the run capture, never from improvement_status: api-contract.md PermitSummary status = status_current as printed (line 404) backed by unpublished_source from the run capture (option iii, decisions.md sections 17 and 20); status_group from the profile mapping of status_current (line 86); open_since from issued or applied date and open_duration_days computed at query time (lines 89-90); is_roofing from the profile classifier. The published records carry permit_number and the confirmed applied, issue, completion and close dates, which the deploy joins to the capture by permit_number
